w:r.w:t: Khushwant Singh is a famous Indian writer.
He writes about his sweet old grandmother.
The grandmother was short, fat, and bent.
She wore a white saree and counted prayer beads.
Her white hair made her look calm and peaceful.
In the village, they were best friends.
She got him ready and walked him to school.
She read holy books and fed chapatis to street dogs.
They moved to the city and their life changed.
He went to an English school by bus.
She could not help him and fed sparrows instead.
He came back from college and she fell sick.
She lay in bed, prayed, and died peacefully.
Her prayer beads fell from her hand.
Thousands of sparrows came and sat near her body.
They did not eat bread and sat in silence.
They flew away quietly when her body was taken.
M. C. Mary Kom is a famous Indian boxer.
She is from a state called Manipur.
Mary Kom came from a very poor family.
Her parents worked hard in fields.
She did boxing in secret because her father disliked it.
She was selected to play a match in the USA.
She did not have money for the plane ticket.
Her father and village friends collected cash for her.
In America, she lost her bags and did not like the food.
She did not give up and played well.
She won a silver medal in her first try.
She worked hard and won many gold medals.
Her life shows that hard work can beat poverty.
She proved that Indian women can win big in sports.
Robert Lynd is a famous Irish writer.
He writes funny stories about everyday habits.
Human memory is actually very good.
People remember phone numbers and actor names.
They remember their daily work easily.
They leave umbrellas and bags on trains.
Sportsmen leave bats and balls behind.
People forget to take their medicine on time.
The author forgets to post letters.
He keeps letters in his pocket for days.
We forget when our mind has other deep thoughts.
A wise man forgets items because he thinks of big things.
A lover forgets because he thinks of his lover.
Forgetting is not always a bad thing.
It does not mean a person is silly.
It shows that the mind is busy with creative thoughts.
E. V. Lucas is a famous English writer.
He writes interesting stories about real life.
A "tight corner" means a very difficult situation.
The author says money trouble is the worst tight corner.
The author went to a big art auction shop.
He had only 63 pounds in his bank.
He did not want to buy anything.
Just for fun, he bid on an expensive painting.
He thought rich people would bid more.
Suddenly, the bidding stopped and he won it for 4,000 pounds.
He was scared because he had no money to pay.
A rich man who missed the shop came to him.
The man bought the painting from him and gave him extra money.
Luck saved the author from a big insult.
He promised never to play foolish games again.
Dr. Arcot Ramasamy Mudaliar was a great Indian lawyer and speaker.
This speech is his advice to young students graduating from college.
A university is not just a place to get degree certificates.
It is a place that prepares students for a better life.
It teaches how to think clearly and choose the right path.
Students must be honest and disciplined in life.
They should read books even after finishing college.
They must always speak the truth and do good work.
The country spends money on your higher education.
So, students must serve the poor and helpless people.
Students should help to make India a strong and peaceful nation.
The country needs good and unselfish leaders.
True leaders work for the happiness of all people.
Education must make students into good citizens and leaders.
The speech teaches us that education is a lifelong duty.
Students must use their knowledge to shine bright and serve the world.
Bill Bryson is a famous American writer.
He writes funny stories about his real travel experiences.
The author gets easily confused when he travels.
He forgets his hotel room numbers and gets lost near toilets.
He cannot do simple things that other people do easily.
Once at an airport, his carry-on bag got stuck.
He pulled it hard, and the zipper broke open completely.
All his things, like coins, newspapers, and tobacco, flew everywhere.
His finger started bleeding, and he panicked in front of everyone. [
He always makes messes inside airplanes.
Once, he knocked over a soft drink onto a lady twice.
Another time, his seat sucked his coat and trapped him.
He even got his mouth covered in black ink while sucking his pen.
Because of his clumsy mistakes, his family stays careful.
His wife asks the kids to cut the food for their father.
He also loses his flyer points because his name is written wrong on tickets.
The story tells us that travel is not fun for everyone.

Gabriel Okara is a famous poet from Nigeria.
He writes about how modern life changes people.
In the old days, people laughed with real joy.
Today, adults smile only with their teeth.
Their eyes stay cold and unfriendly.
People are not true friends anymore.
They shake hands but look at your money.
They say "come again" but lock their doors.
The father also learned to be fake.
He changes his face like changing clothes.
He has different smiles for work and parties.
He looks at his small son's innocent face.
He feels bad about his own fake smiles.
He wants to forget his bad adult habits.
The father asks his son to teach him.
He wants to learn how to laugh naturally again.
He wants his pure childhood heart back.
Ogden Nash is a famous American poet.
He writes funny poems about people.
The poet loves to watch sports.
He does not want to play games.
He is happy to be a fan in the stands.
Athletes run fast and play hard.
They play football, hockey, and basketball.
The poet likes them but will not swap places.
They hurt their knees, hands, and faces.
They do not care about hurting others.
The poet's body wants to stay safe.
He likes to sit, eat, and drink with friends.
He pays for tickets but stays off the field.
Some people play and some people watch.
The poet accepts his role happily.
He chooses comfort over sports fame.
William Wordsworth is a great English poet.
People call him the "Poet of Nature."
The poet sits under some trees in spring.
He looks around at the beautiful world.
He sees lovely flowers and green trees breathing fresh air.
Every living thing in nature is happy.
Small birds hop and play around him.
Tree branches open up to catch the wind.
This beautiful scene makes the poet sad.
He feels bad about how humans fight and hurt each other.
The poet believes God made nature to be happy.
Nature wants all creatures to live in peace.
Humans are sad because they do not follow nature.
Nature is a place of true joy and peace.
Humans must stop wars and live in love.
T. S. Eliot is a very famous English poet.
He wrote this funny poem about a cat.
Macavity is a mystery cat called the "Hidden Paw."
He is a master criminal who does bad things.
He never leaves any footprints or clues behind.
Macavity breaks human laws and the law of gravity.
He can float in the air without falling down.
The London police can never catch him.
Macavity is a very tall, thin ginger cat.
His eyes are sunken in, and his brow is deep in thought.
His coat is dirty and his whiskers are messy.
He moves his head side to side like a snake.
When he looks half-asleep, he is wide awake.
He looks like a normal cat but he is an evil monster inside.
Macavity always escapes from the crime scene.
The poem uses fun lines to show an uncatchable criminal cat.
5. Everest Is Not The Only Peak (Poem)
Kulothungan is the pen name of Professor V. C. Kulandaiswamy.
He is a famous Tamil scholar and poet who wrote in English too.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain, but it is not the only peak.
Every small hill has its own beauty and height.
Similarly, you do not need to be the topmost person to be successful.
Doing small work with honesty is better than doing big, wrong work.
We must respect people who work hard every day.
Reaching a lower peak with self-respect is a grand victory.
A person's value is not measured by money or position.
It is measured by their good character and dedication.
We must adore people who do their duties perfectly.
We should never feel low if we fail to reach the top.
We must stand tall and feel proud of our honest efforts.
are the true peaks of human life.
The poem tells us to appreciate every honest human effort.
Every good human being is a winner in life.
William Shakespeare is the world-famous English playwright and poet.
This poem is a small part from his famous history play
King Richard is very sad because he lost his power.
He tells his friends to sit on the ground and talk about dead kings.
Some kings were killed in war, and some were poisoned by wives.
Death is the supreme king over all human rulers.
Death sits inside the hollow crown of a mortal king.
Death laughs at the king's false power and high pride.
A crown looks big but it is hollow (empty) inside.
It gives a king a small time to act like a god on earth.
At the end, Death comes with a small pin, breaks the castle wall, and kills the king.
The king tells his friends not to bow or respect him anymore.
He says he is just a normal human being who needs bread and feels pain.
He has tastes, wants, and needs friends just like ordinary people.
The poem shows that death treats kings and beggars the same way.
Power and crowns are temporary, but death is permanent.

Exam Passage: The Life of Honeybees

Honeybees are highly social insects that live in well-organized colonies called beehives. A single hive can contain up to 60,000 bees, divided into three distinct types: the Queen, the Workers, and the Drones. The Queen is the largest bee and is responsible for laying thousands of eggs daily. The female Worker bees do all the actual work, such as collecting pollen from flowers, building the honeycomb, and protecting the hive from enemies. The male Drones exist solely to mate with the queen. Bees communicate with each other using a special series of movements known as the "waggle dance," which tells other hive members the exact location of food sources.
What are the three types of bees found in a beehive?
The three types of bees found in a beehive are the Queen, the Workers, and the Drones.
What is the main responsibility of the Queen bee?
The main responsibility of the Queen bee is to lay thousands of eggs daily.
Mention any two duties performed by the female Worker bees.
Two duties performed by the Worker bees are collecting pollen from flowers and protecting the hive from enemies.
How do honeybees communicate the location of food sources to one another?
Honeybees communicate the location of food sources using a special series of movements known as the "waggle dance."
Find a word in the passage which means "groups of insects living together."
